components.name: TileLayout
components.role: Binary space-partition (BSP) tree that owns pane geometry; every Split node has exactly 2 children (first/second), a Direction (Horizontal/Vertical), and an f32 ratio clamped 0.1-0.9. No native N-ary column primitive.

components.name: TabBarView / header hit-areas
components.role: Computes a Vec<Rect> of clickable hit-areas per open tab plus scroll-left/scroll-right/new-tab buttons every frame; header is a dynamic N-item button system, not a fixed slot count.

components.name: ViewState
components.role: Central per-frame hit-area registry (tab_hit_areas, sidebar_tab_hit_areas, project_row_areas, mobile_menu_hit_area, pane_infos, split_borders, etc.) consumed by the mouse-input layer.

components.name: ProjectRowArea / sidebar row hit-test
components.role: Lays out one Rect per sidebar row (or MULTIPLE disjoint Rects for a single logical row, e.g. project-header + right-aligned '+' new-chat button) and dispatches clicks via exact (col,row) containment scan + ProjectRowKind match.

components.name: ContextMenuKind / right-click menu
components.role: State-driven floating popup menu (Workspace/GitWorkspace/Tab/Pane/ProjectNewChat variants) whose item list changes based on selection/worktree state; rendered as an overlay Rect at click (x,y), not embedded in the header.

components.name: Plugin pane runtime (Overlay/Split/Tab/Zoomed)
components.role: Realizes a manifest [[panes]] entry by spawning the plugin's own argv command as a real PTY-backed subprocess pane inserted into the host TileLayout BSP tree (split_pane_argv_command / spawn_overlay_argv_command).

components.name: Plugin action contexts / dispatch surface
components.role: manifest_actions() iterator exposes plugin [[actions]] (with PluginActionContext: Global/Workspace/Tab/Pane/Selection) ONLY through the JSON API/CLI layer; not referenced anywhere in the ratatui UI render/hit-test layer.

components.name: src/selection.rs (terminal text selection)
components.role: Single-pane character/word text-selection for clipboard copy (Anchor/Dragging/Done phases) — NOT a multi-row/file selection or bulk-action model.

claims.claim: TileLayout is a strict binary space-partition tree: Node enum is Pane(PaneId) | Split{direction, ratio, first: Box<Node>, second: Box<Node>} — always exactly two children per split, ratio clamped to 0.1..0.9 by valid_split_ratio(). There is no native N-ary/Miller-column primitive in the engine.

Miller-columns-style N-parallel-column browsing (e.g. parent|current|preview or a deeper chain) IS achievable on top of TileLayout by chaining Horizontal binary splits — e.g. split A|BC then split BC into B|C yields 3 side-by-side columns. Demonstrated directly by the test fixture sample_layout(), which nests Horizontal/Vertical/Horizontal splits to produce 4 simultaneous panes with independent ratios.

split_rect() computes each column's pixel width purely as round(area.width * ratio) with NO minimum-width floor beyond the 0.1-0.9 ratio clamp; with many chained columns on a narrow terminal, individual column widths can shrink to a few cells or less.

The header/tab-bar already computes an independent, mouse-clickable Vec<Rect> hit-area per open tab (TabBarView.tab_hit_areas) plus separate scroll-left, scroll-right, and new-tab button rects, all stored in ViewState and re-derived every frame by compute_tab_bar_view(). This proves the header supports an arbitrary, dynamically-sized set of functional buttons, not a hardcoded fixed count.

layout_tab_hit_areas() lays out hit-rects in a loop bounded only by available pixel width (breaks when x >= right), i.e. the number of clickable header buttons is elastic, not capped by an enum/array size.

Row-right buttons are an EXISTING, live, shipped pattern: compute_project_row_areas() splits a single logical sidebar row (a Project header) into TWO disjoint Rects on the same row: a main name/collapse-chevron area and a fixed-width (3-cell) '+' new-chat button pinned to the row's right edge. Inline code comment explicitly states this is done 'to keep hit-test unambiguous'.

Mouse dispatch for sidebar rows (project_row_kind_at + toggle_projects_row_at) does an exact (col,row) containment scan over Vec<ProjectRowArea> and match()es on ProjectRowKind::{Project, Chat, Empty, More, NewChat}, each triggering a distinct action — confirming the architecture is a generic list of (Rect, tag) hit-areas per row, trivially extensible to add more row-right action buttons (e.g. a rename/delete icon) by pushing an additional ProjectRowArea per row.

A full state-driven right-click context-menu system exists: ContextMenuKind enum (Workspace, GitWorkspace{is_linked_worktree, has_worktree_children, collapsed}, Tab, Pane, ProjectNewChat{has_workspace}) whose .items() label list is computed dynamically per-variant/per-state (e.g. GitWorkspace menu items differ for linked-worktree vs has-children-collapsed vs plain).

The context menu renders as a floating popup Rect positioned at the recorded click (x,y) via app.context_menu_rect(), drawn by render_context_menu() as a separate overlay widget — it is NOT integrated into the persistent header/tab-bar region. Today's 'context-aware UI' is popup-menu-on-click, not a Windows-Explorer-style toolbar strip that morphs in place based on selection.

The only 'Selection' concept implemented in the codebase (src/selection.rs) is single-pane terminal TEXT selection (Anchor -> Dragging -> Done phases, screen-buffer row/col coordinates, OSC-52 clipboard copy) for copying terminal output — unrelated to a Finder-style multi-row/file selection with a bulk-action toolbar. No 'selected_rows'/'multi_select' style field was found on ViewState or AppState during this audit.

claims.claim: Plugin manifests (herdr-plugin.toml) declare [[actions]] (id, title, description?, contexts: Vec<PluginActionContext>, platforms?, command), [[events]] (on, command), [[panes]] (id, title, placement: PluginPanePlacement, command), and [[link_handlers]] (id, title, pattern regex, action). PluginActionContext = {Global, Workspace, Tab, Pane, Selection}. PluginPanePlacement = {Overlay(default), Split, Tab, Zoomed}.

A plugin pane is realized by spawning the plugin's own declared argv command as a REAL PTY-backed subprocess pane inserted directly into the host's TileLayout BSP tree (open_plugin_split_pane calls ws.split_pane_argv_command; open_plugin_overlay_pane calls spawn_overlay_argv_command). It becomes an ordinary layout pane like any terminal pane — it is NOT a native ratatui widget sharing herdr's own render tree, mouse hit-area registry, or ViewState.

Plugin-declared [[actions]] are exposed ONLY through the JSON API/CLI layer (manifest_actions() iterator feeding PluginActionList/PluginActionInvoke API methods). A recursive grep for PluginActionInfo | ContextMenuKind::Plugin | plugin_actions_for across src/ui/ (all 15 files), src/app/state.rs, and src/app/input/ returned ZERO matches. This means plugins today CANNOT contribute native header buttons, context-menu items, or sidebar rows to the herdr TUI itself — their only UI-adjacent surfaces are (a) an embedded subprocess pane (Overlay/Split/Tab/Zoomed) and (b) actions/link-handlers triggerable via external API/CLI, not rendered inline by herdr's own chrome.

claims.component_note: supporting architectural constraint from project rules, not code
claims.claim: Project-level architecture guardrail (AGENTS.md, upstream/read-only) explicitly classifies 'sidebar, row, card, or widget' state as TUI/client presentation state (not shared server/runtime state), and instructs that new UI-surface behavior should not be added to the shared server/API protocol unless it's a genuinely shared runtime fact. This supports building a file manager as a core TUI/client-side Rust feature (extending ViewState/sidebar.rs/mouse.rs/layout.rs) rather than as a plugin (external subprocess) or as new server-protocol surface.
